parts.t: Fort Langley is a village on the Fraser River, with shops, restaurants, museums and trails, and the Hudson’s Bay Company fort that is now a national historic site. The village core is a heritage conservation area, so the rules for a property matter as much as the house.

Written by Jared Gibbons, REALTOR®, Royal LePage Little Oak Realty, on October 8, 2026. I have worked in Fraser Valley real estate for 11+ years. Facts come from the official sources noted on this page. Rules and boundaries change, so confirm anything important with the Township of Langley.
Not legal, planning or financial advice. Confirm zoning, plan designations and school catchments before you buy or sell.

blocks.text: Heritage and planning in Fort Langley

parts.t: Fort Langley’s heritage rules shape what owners can change, so check them before you buy.
The Fort Langley Community Plan was adopted in 1987 and made the downtown a heritage alteration permit area.
The downtown became a heritage conservation area in 1997.
Changes in a heritage conservation area generally need a Heritage Alteration Permit.
The Township’s OCP update includes draft directions for a community plan covering Aldergrove, Fort Langley, Murrayville, Northwest Langley and Walnut Grove.

Why is Fort Langley called the birthplace of BC?
The act establishing the colony of British Columbia was proclaimed at Fort Langley on November 19, 1858.
Is Fort Langley a heritage area?
Yes. Fort Langley is one of only two heritage conservation areas in the Township, and changes there generally need a Heritage Alteration Permit.
Some low areas can. During the 2023 freshet the Township issued a flood advisory for unprotected floodplain areas including Fort Langley. Check the exact property.
Which schools are in Fort Langley?
Fort Langley Elementary and Langley Fine Arts School have Fort Langley addresses. Check the SD35 School Locator for the exact address.

Is there camping near Fort Langley?
Yes, in two regional parks. Derby Reach has the Edgewater Bar Campground with 38 sites, and Brae Island, across the Jacob Haldi Bridge, has Fort Camping, open year-round.
